A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MR-GSM8K benchmark and evaluation framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive restructuring and a changed title.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, diagnostic fine-tuning results, and comparisons of human and automatic grading in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports original evaluations across fourteen models, zero-shot and three-shot comparisons, and a demonstration-composition ablation. Original fine-tuning and grading-validation results also remain in the appendices.

M1.justification: The question-solution diagnostic procedure, MetaMath-7B solution generation, and correctness/error-step/error-reason tasks remain unchanged. GPT-4-generated diagnostic training and Llama2 QLoRA fine-tuning are retained in Appendix B. Revised model selection and prompting conditions concern evaluation settings rather than a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use English GSM8K problems, their Program-of-Thought and reversed variants, and GSM8K-based diagnostic training data. New evaluated models, demonstration configurations, and revised sample counts do not introduce additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The primary comparison in Table 2 is substantially revised: v4 introduces Llama3, Phi3, Qwen, DeepSeek, and Claude3 models, evaluates GPT-4-Turbo, and replaces WizardMath-70B there with WizardMath-v1.1-7B. MAmmoTH-70B and MetaMath-70B remain. Earlier comparators are partly retained in the automatic-grading comparison, but v3's GSM8K-only fine-tuned Llama2 control disappears.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation temperature changes from 0.5 to zero. Whereas v3 primarily uses zero-shot commercial-model evaluation and three-shot specialized-model evaluation, v4 tests every main-table model under both conditions and varies demonstration correctness in an additional experiment. Table 1 also revises the reported dataset from 3,000 instances to 2,999, with correct/incorrect counts changing from 1,427/1,573 to 1,428/1,571; this count revision is unexplained.

E4.justification: v4 adds systematic zero-shot versus three-shot analysis and an ablation varying the number of correct demonstrations for Phi3 and two Llama3 models (Figure 6). Appendix D revises the reasoning-failure cases. Conversely, v3's GSM8K transfer check and several successful-diagnosis examples disappear. Diagnostic fine-tuning and human-versus-automatic grading analyses remain after relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for benchmark performance. v4's statement that zero temperature minimizes variance does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v4 Table 2 contains extensive new results, including GPT-4-Turbo MR-Scores of 50.5/53.0 and Llama3-70B scores of 38.3/34.2 for zero/three shots. These are updated experiments, not same-setting gains over v3's GPT4 score of 0.495, because models and settings differ. Table 1 adds length and step statistics. The grading-validation results remain unchanged, while v3's GSM8K fine-tuning results of 74.3% and 74.9% are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain mathematically equivalent definitions of MCC, error-step accuracy, error-reason accuracy, and weighted MR-Score. No new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear. Omission of the numerical score weights is a documentation loss, without evidence that the underlying formula changed.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the meta-reasoning paradigm, MR-GSM8K, and MR-Score. v4 strengthens benchmark transformation into an explicit contribution claiming robustness against overfitting and contamination, and adds the introductory finding that much smaller models can outperform larger ones. These extend the claims without replacing the paper's central thesis.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning model size versus data quality, demonstration-induced prediction bias, and equation-equivalence and unit errors. Appendix A introduces a substantive applicability limitation for holistic or creative subjects. The earlier RLHF/sycophancy explanation and discussion of diagnostic fine-tuning failing to improve GSM8K are removed. The broader critique of learning only correct solution paths remains.

D1.justification: v4 adds a few-shot prompt, a partial annotation manual with detailed handling rules and examples, and annotator-training and supervision details. It removes v3's explicit MR-Score weights of 0.2/0.3/0.5, benchmark repository URL, Chinese translation workflow, and explicit assurance of manual error-reason grading for the main results. These substantially alter reproducibility documentation; the missing URL does not establish withdrawal of the repository.

R1.justification: v4 adds model-related references and contamination-focused work by Balloccu et al. and Yang et al., while removing discussions and citations concerning Orca 2, sycophancy, imitation, and some reasoning-training approaches. The principal positioning against result-oriented math benchmarks and existing solution-judgment work remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental narrative, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Dataset construction and evaluation metrics become separate sections; annotation material moves into the main text, while fine-tuning and limitations move into reorganized appendices. The title changes from 'Meta-Reasoning Revolution' to 'Meta-Reasoning Benchmark.'

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. Table 2 gains model-size groupings and paired shot-setting columns, Table 1 gains descriptive-statistics columns, and Figure 1 is redesigned for the expanded model comparison. v4 adds an ablation chart, removes v3's diagnostic-performance charts, and repackages or relocates prompts, cases, and retained illustrations.

improvement.justification: Paired zero-shot/three-shot evaluations and comparisons of general versus specialized models make the benchmark evidence more informative than v3's largely separate model/shot groups. The demonstration-composition ablation and annotation manual further improve scrutiny. These provide a limited net gain, tempered by missing score weights and repository access information, removal of the GSM8K transfer control, and stronger contamination-robustness claims without a dedicated contamination test.
